caveat: All three aggregators likely derive from one self-reported profile, and the only real news — TheNextWeb on their 2011 TechStars Boston demo day — states no founding year. strohlmedical.com returns no content and the trail stops around 2012. In scope: NeuroEPG, an evoked-potential device for stroke triage.

name: Biosensics
evidence: "Founded in 2007 by three scientists from Harvard University, BioSensics has pioneered the use of wearable sensors and digital health technologies in healthcare and clinical research."
caveat: Stated on the live homepage; /about-us/ is a 404. In scope: wearable sensors and digital biomarkers explicitly focused on neurological and rare disorders.

name: Intratech Medical
evidence: Tracxn, PitchBook and CB Insights give 2007, founder Eran Levit, Netanya.
caveat: No primary confirmation; Startup Nation Central returned 403. intratechmedical.com returns no content. In scope: NAVIMAX, a spiral balloon catheter for clot retrieval in acute ischaemic stroke, CE marked May 2014. The company may have moved to Kibbutz Shefayim.

name: Neural-FLEX
evidence: 易念科技（深圳）有限公司成立于2018年 — Yinian Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. established 2018, self-developing BCI technology. Address matches the Shenzhen address on neu-flex.com exactly.
caveat: From a Chinese healthcare-industry media database rather than the SAIC register. In scope: the SOULINK non-invasive EEG headband, EEG and EMG wearables, depression-warning models. neu-flex.com returned HTTP 521 on every attempt.

name: Oncomfort
evidence: Company boilerplate in its own Series A release: "Oncomfort, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Wavre near Brussels (Belgium)..." Founders Diane Jooris, Mario Huyghe and Julien Tesse.
caveat: LOCATION: Wavre, not Brussels, per its own boilerplate. ACQUIRED by HypnoVR of Strasbourg in October 2023 — and HypnoVR is itself a row in this index, so the two are one company since then. oncomfort.com fails DNS.

name: Nuro Corp
evidence: Company timeline entry: "2017 - NURO is incorporated".
conflict: The same page frames a 2014 origin and one secondary source says the company was "first conceived in 2014 in Waterloo and delivered in 2017". 2014 is an origin story rather than a founding, and the company labels 2017 as incorporation.

name: Mr. Doc
evidence: Italian register: MR DOC S.R.L., P.IVA 14786521006, Rome; registered from 22/05/2018, trading from 01/07/2018, innovative startup from 21/09/2018.
caveat: SCOPE: AI diagnostics from noisy consumer-device signals covering arrhythmias, hypertension, asthma, COPD and Parkinson's, plus retinal OCT — general AI diagnostics where the nervous system is one target among many. Two similarly named Rome entities exist and only the CORDIS-coordinator match was confirmed. The LinkedIn slug suggests a rebrand to "Cardiia", unverified.

name: Psicologia Viva
evidence: "O Psicologia Viva foi fundado em 2015, em Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais."
conflict: CNPJ 28.567.713/0001-50 sits in a range consistent with a 2017 registration, so the legal entity is probably younger than the 2015 founding. Every Brazilian CNPJ mirror returned 402 or 403, so the registry date is unverified.

name: Bionic Vision Technologies
evidence: "the University of Melbourne-led consortium (later named Bionic Vision Australia or BVA and, in 2016, Bionic Vision Technologies Pty Ltd) received $42 million over four years."
caveat: The consortium and the company are different things: Bionic Vision Australia ran 2010-2016 as an ARC-funded research consortium and ceased operations on 31 December 2016; Bionic Vision Technologies Pty Ltd is the 2016 commercial spinout. 2010 must not be used. bionicvis.com now redirects to polonorterestaurant.com — the domain has lapsed and been resold.

name: Cambridge Humanae
evidence: Companies House: CAMBRIDGE HUMANAE LTD, company 09909565, incorporated 9 December 2015; DISSOLVED 3 March 2020.
caveat: An incorporation date with no company-authored history to check against — there is no website. The registered address, 71-75 Shelton Street, Covent Garden, is a mass virtual-office address, so the London location says little. SCOPE: psychometrics plus AI assessing stress resilience in high-risk roles, with no nervous-system measurement.

name: Neeuro
evidence: "Neeuro is a global company, founded in 2013 in Singapore, which specialises in the utilisation of Brain-Computer Interface technology." Founders Eddie Chau and Alvin Chan.
caveat: In scope: the SenzeBand EEG headband, NeeuroOS analytics and digital therapeutics for attention. Neeuro's own about page states no founding year, and the Temasek-linked-roots claim could not be confirmed from any source.

name: Brainboost Neurofeedack
evidence: brainboost described as founded in February 2016 under medical direction, founder Philipp Heiler, a licensed physician.
caveat: The index name is misspelled and the domain has moved to brainboost.de, which states no founding year. Two linked entities exist: a Munich neurofeedback medical practice, which is a clinic and out of scope, and brainboost, which does R&D, sells EEG hardware and its BrainAssistant software and franchises a turnkey concept. A clinic-plus-franchise hybrid.

name: Movement Disorders Diagnostic Technologies (MDDT)
evidence: Tracxn gives 2013, founders Mandar Jog and Jack Lee. An Ontario Brain Institute grant to MDDT is dated June 2013 and Lee was an OBI Entrepreneur in the 2013 class.
conflict: Not about the year: this row and "MDDT inc" at the same mddtinc.ca domain are the same company and should be merged. The OBI grant and cohort confirm existence by mid-2013 but are funding dates, not a founding statement.

name: Divergence Neuro
evidence: Corporations Canada: Divergence Neuro Technologies Inc., incorporated 3 October 2020, Toronto. Directors Boris Gernega, Alex Ni, Randy Knudson, Jeff Moore.
caveat: An incorporation date; the company's own site states no founding year and its /about path 404s. The legal name is Divergence Neuro Technologies Inc. In scope: a cloud neurofeedback and biofeedback platform covering EEG, HRV, respiration and skin conductance.

name: B. Braun
evidence: "It all began in 1839, when Julius Wilhelm Braun bought the Rose Pharmacy in Melsungen."
caveat: The year belongs to the GROUP, B. Braun Melsungen AG of Germany. The index records Bethlehem, USA, which is B. Braun Medical Inc., a distinct and much later subsidiary — one of the two fields is wrong. SCOPE: a general medical and pharmaceutical company spanning infusion, dialysis, surgical and wound care with 5,000+ products; neuro exposure is confined to the Aesculap division's neurosurgery instruments.

name: Cerebriu
evidence: Founded 2018, Copenhagen; founders Robert Lauritzen, Akshay Pai, Erik B. Dam, Mads Nielsen, Martin Lillholm; first funding August 2018.
caveat: Consistent across every source but with no primary confirmation: cerebriu.com/about is a 404 and /who-we-are states no year. The founder list points to a University of Copenhagen image-analysis origin. In scope: Apollo, a CE-marked real-time brain-MRI triage and protocol-optimisation tool.

name: Effectivate
evidence: "Effectivate was established in 2018 by Shai Granot (Founder & CEO) and Anna Izotcheev (Co-Founder & Chief Science Officer)."
caveat: The index URL effectivate.org redirects to the Hebrew site; the English site is effectivate.com. SCOPE: software brain-training and cognitive exercises for adults 55+, with no EEG, sensing or neural measurement.

name: HOZ Medical
evidence: 华志微创医疗科技（北京）有限公司 established 2017-01-20, registered capital 14.29M yuan, legal representative Zhang Weigang, website hozmedical.com.
caveat: A registration date from Chinese business-registry data; the underlying robot technology lineage is older. In scope: frameless stereotactic neurosurgery robots deployed in 100+ hospitals. hozmedical.com refused connection on both HTTP and HTTPS.

name: Heraeus
evidence: In 1851 Wilhelm Carl Heraeus took over the Einhorn Pharmacy in Hanau from his father and developed it into the family business; the platinum melting works followed from 1856.
caveat: The year belongs to Heraeus Holding GmbH, a 175-year-old precious-metals and technology conglomerate spanning platinum, quartz glass, sensors, dental and photovoltaics. The index URL points at a product page for implantable electrodes belonging to Heraeus Medical Components, one business unit — a component supplier to neurostimulation OEMs rather than a neurotechnology company.

name: Secure Nest
evidence: Startup Daily, 22 November 2018: "The pair began working together in late 2015 to identify therapy tools that could be digitised."
caveat: The date is when the co-founders began working together; the platform launched publicly around 2018 after three years of development. SCOPE: an online schema therapy platform for therapists and clients — secure diary storage, forms and progress charts. No sensing or measurement. Founded by Sally and Joseph Skewes in South Australia with Michiel van Vreeswijk.

name: Redenlab
evidence: "Redenlab is a neuroscience clinical outcome assessment technology company founded in 2017." Tracxn independently concurs.
caveat: In scope: speech and voice acoustic analysis as a digital biomarker for neurodegenerative disease, used as a clinical outcome assessment in trials. Founded by Adam P. Vogel, who directs the Centre for Neuroscience of Speech at Melbourne.

name: Saintrino Technologies Inc
evidence: Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, Apollo and Dealroom give 2010, Longueuil, Quebec; specialties "Brain Computer Interfaces, Bio-Technology, Neuro Ergonomy".
conflict: The company's own site carries a 2013 copyright, which does not corroborate 2010, and says Montreal rather than the Longueuil the index and aggregators give. Crunchbase returned 403, so even the aggregator figure is second-hand. The site brands itself "St-RINO Technologies"; the Quebec REQ would settle it.

name: Integrated Listening Systems
evidence: "iLs was founded in Denver, CO in 2007 as the first neurotechnology company to systematically integrate music, movement and language exercises for the purpose of improving brain function." Founders Kate O'Brien Minson, Randall Redfield and Ron Minson.
caveat: Now part of Unyte Health; the index URL redirects into the parent's site and the standalone about page is gone, which is why the year comes from the Australian regional site. Ron Minson trained in the Tomatis Method around 1990 and Redfield began collaborating in 2005 — neither is the company. A therapy programme rather than a measuring or stimulating device.

name: Aifred Health
evidence: Company origin story: the founders entered the IBM Watson AI XPRIZE "in late 2016" and incorporated "the following year as a condition of continuing in the competition—and Aifred Health was born." Founders David Benrimoh, Kelly Perlman, Sonia Israel, Robert Fratila.
caveat: By the company's own telling 2017 is an incorporation forced by a competition rule, with the team forming late 2016; 2017 is the date the company itself claims. In scope: AI clinical decision support for selecting depression treatments, out of McGill. Took second place and US$1M in the XPRIZE final.

name: Moodru
evidence: Crunchbase gives 11 September 2018, California; a VR health-tech company building immersive environments for phobias and DBT adherence.
caveat: Unverifiable independently: moodru.com returns 403 and every trace routes back to a single Crunchbase profile with no news, funding announcement or institutional mention. A day-level date like this often reflects an incorporation filing. Beware Moodfit, a separate Palo Alto mood-tracking company.

name: Impact Applications Inc.
evidence: Company timeline: 1994, Dr Mark Lovell develops a computerized neurocognitive test "which becomes the basis for his company, Neurohealth"; 2002, Drs Collins and Lovell officially incorporate Neurohealth as ImPACT Applications, Inc.
conflict: 1994 is when the predecessor company Neurohealth was established, which is arguably when the company came into existence; 2002 is the re-incorporation and rename, and the year the company's own about page gives. The 1994 predecessor must not be dropped silently.

name: Cogwear
evidence: "Year Established 2018", corroborated by a statement that "Cogwear, LLC, was born in May 2018 with support from the Penn Center for Innovation" and by Tracxn and CB Insights giving 2018 with founders Michael Platt and Arjun Ramakrishnan.
caveat: A University of Pennsylvania spinout making dry-electrode wearable EEG headbands, with NSF and NIH support — squarely in scope. Penn Center for Innovation confirms the spinout but states no year. The index URL is wrong: the live site is cogweartech.com, not cogweartechnologies.com.

name: Braze Mobility
evidence: "Founded in 2016, Braze Mobility provides effective navigation for wheelchair users."
caveat: The URL in the index, /about-us/, is a 404; the live page is /about-braze-mobility/. SCOPE: blind-spot ultrasonic sensors and cameras bolted onto powered wheelchairs, with audio, visual and haptic alerts. Assistive mobility hardware with no neural interface; the adjacency is that its users often have neurological conditions.

name: Neurolens (eyeBrain Medical)
evidence: CB Insights and Crunchbase both give 2012 for the eyeBrain Medical entity. No primary company page stating the year was reachable.
caveat: The year belongs to eyeBrain Medical Inc., the original name, and the row is TWO renames behind: eyeBrain Medical became Neurolens and then Newton as of September 2025. LOCATION: Coppell, Texas, earlier Costa Mesa; Sioux Falls appears to be where investor Bluestem Capital sits. SCOPE: contoured-prism prescription lenses sold through optometrists, with a trigeminal-nerve-stress hypothesis in the marketing — optometry, not neurotechnology.

name: RoboKind
evidence: Tracxn gives 2011, founders David Hanson, Richard Margolin and Fred Margolin, Dallas; Golden agrees.
caveat: The company's own founder page and its EdTech Digest profile tell the origin story but state no year, so this rests on aggregators. Co-founded by David Hanson of Hanson Robotics; the Milo robot descends from their Zeno R25. SCOPE: a two-foot expressive humanoid delivering a social-skills curriculum to autistic children — educational robotics, nothing measuring or modulating the nervous system.

name: Saccade Analytics
evidence: Crunchbase, CB Insights and Dealroom give 2016; the company's own about page was indexed as saying it was founded in the fall of 2016 by Isabel Galiana and Prof. Henrietta "Mimi" Galiana, though that page could not be opened.
caveat: Genuinely in scope: VR eye and head tracking running oculomotor and vestibular batteries in 3-12 minutes for concussion assessment, out of about thirty years of Mimi Galiana's research at McGill; trialled by World Rugby in March 2021. RENAMED to NeuroFlex at neuroflex.io, and saccadeanalytics.com now fails DNS. A Creative Destruction Lab 2017/18 cohort entry is an accelerator date, not a founding.

name: NeuCogni
evidence: Crunchbase and Apollo list 2018; a blog post covering the wearable is dated May 2018.
caveat: A May 2018 mention means founding was 2018 OR EARLIER, so 2018 may be an import artefact. neucogni.com redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page and the only surviving presence is a free site-builder page. In scope: a transcranial neurostimulation wearable, team Simon Chatzigiannis and Sahil and Sanil Doshi, address in Fords, New Jersey — no source connects the company to Trinidad and Tobago, which the index also records.

name: Brain Vision LLC
evidence: Brain Products GmbH states that Brain Vision LLC began operating in 2005 as a one-person office in Herndon, Virginia, and was its first fully owned subsidiary, established to introduce Brain Products solutions to North American researchers.
caveat: Not merely a distributor but a WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARY of Brain Products GmbH of Gilching, and also reseller for BESA, CGX, CREmedical and Easycap. The 2005 year belongs to the US subsidiary; the German parent has its own earlier founding in the late 1990s. A sales and support organisation rather than a developer.

name: Journey Live
evidence: "Founded in 2015, Journey also operates corporate programs in 15 cities around the world." Secondary sources specify March 2015, after founder Stephen Sokoler sold his previous company Altrum in September 2014.
caveat: SCOPE: began as live-streamed group meditation classes and corporate mindfulness, and has pivoted to a B2B employee-assistance and mental-health benefits platform. No EEG, no biometrics, no sensing hardware. Its about page headline reads "11 Years, 11 Million Lives Touched", a relative phrase that was not used.

name: DiamPark
evidence: French register: DIAMPARK SAS, SIREN 883 799 645, RCS Nanterre, created by notarial deed 21 February 2020; activity R&D in biotechnology.
conflict: The register gives 2020 as incorporation while aggregator and press descriptions say "founded in 2021"; the company's own site has no history page to arbitrate.

name: UpSurgeOn
evidence: "UpSurgeOn S.R.L. was established in 2017 as a MedTech Company headquartered in Milan. At its foundation, the company comprised a team of 5 members."
caveat: Some secondary sources say 2015; the company's own page explains the gap, since founders Federico Nicolosi and Giannantonio Spena pioneered 3D surgical planning models from 2014 but the entity dates from 2017. In scope: neurosurgical simulation and training, physical anatomical simulators plus an AR academy app.

name: Petal Technology
evidence: Petal Technology LLC founded 2016 by Dan Schmitz and James Glazer in Chicago; HQ relocated to Austin in 2019.
caveat: A StartupCity profile has Schmitz starting with off-the-shelf components in 2015, suggesting tinkering earlier than formation. petal.tech is live and genuinely the right company: Metrics, a real-time neural data toolkit streaming EEG from Muse headsets — in scope. LOCATION: founded in Chicago, not the Austin the index records.

name: ai4medicine
evidence: Startbase, a German startup database, lists ai4medicine of Berlin as founded 2018; legal entity ai4Medicine UG, founders Dietmar Frey and Michelle Livne. Tracxn, Crunchbase and EU-Startups concur.
caveat: No primary or institutional statement found, and the index stores only a LinkedIn URL because there is no working standalone site. In scope: AI decision support for acute stroke treatment; co-founder Dietmar Frey was a neurosurgeon at Charite. At least one source indicates the company is no longer active, unverified against the Handelsregister.

name: Edvince
evidence: "Lars Edvinsson founded Edvince in 2003 under the name Pronas Pharma and served as chairman of the Company until May 2016."
caveat: RENAMED: founded as Pronas Pharma, so the 2003 date belongs to that entity. SCOPE: a DRUG developer — pharmaceutical candidates keeping cerebral vessels open after stroke and subarachnoid haemorrhage, from Prof. Lars Edvinsson's Lund University vascular research. SmiLe classifies its product type as "Drugs".

name: Syngli
evidence: Communitech, the Waterloo region tech hub: Syngli founded 2014, "formerly known as NeuRecall Inc.", offices in Kitchener-Waterloo and Berkeley, software "inspired by cognitive neuroscience and machine learning".
caveat: RENAMED from NeuRecall Inc. SCOPE: syngli.com serves an e-learning platform with interactive courses and performance tracking; the neuro connection is the cognitive-science inspiration behind its spaced-learning engine and the original name, not any hardware or signal measurement.

name: Awake Labs
evidence: Gust and PitchBook both list 2015. UBC Sauder states the company "was formed out of UBC Sauder's New Venture Design class by two UBC engineering graduates - Paul Fijal and Andrea Palmer", without giving a year.
caveat: No founding year appears anywhere on awakelabs.com. A 2021 UBC alumni profile says only "Six years later", a relative phrase that was not used. In scope: a wearable measuring heart rate, skin temperature and electrodermal activity to detect anxiety in autistic people. LOCATION: originated in Vancouver at UBC; Toronto is defensible for the present day but not the founding.

name: Fisher Wallace
evidence: "The company was founded in 2007 by entrepreneur Charles Avery Fisher, son of electronics pioneer Avery Fisher, and Martin Wallace."
caveat: The device predates the company and that trap is real here: Fisher Wallace ACQUIRED the cranial electrotherapy stimulation device from Saul and Bernard Liss in 2006, and the Lisses already held FDA 510(k) clearance, so any pre-2007 date belongs to them. The company's own about pages 404. Co-founder Martin Wallace died shortly after formation.

name: MindProber Labs
evidence: MRWeb Daily Research News states MindProber was established in 2016; the same article reports the rename.
caveat: RENAMED to Mediaprobe, announced 5 June 2023, repositioning away from its neuroscience framing toward general media analytics — so both the row name and the URL are stale. In scope while it lasted: second-by-second electrodermal activity via hand-held sensors in respondents' homes, producing an "Emotional Impact Score".

name: Bionik Labaratories
evidence: The 10-K corporate history states Bionik Canada was incorporated 24 March 2011 under the Canada Business Corporations Act, and the Delaware entity was renamed Bionik Laboratories Corp. effective 13 February 2015.
conflict: Aggregators say 2009 against the filing's 2011, which is an incorporation date; founders Michal Prywata and Thiago Caires were Ryerson students who may date the venture earlier. Separately, Bionik acquired Interactive Motion Technologies in 2016 and IMT — the MIT-derived originator of the InMotion robots — is substantially older, so an IMT-era date must not land on this row.

name: Mentem - brain training
evidence: Czech commercial register, ICO 03514161: established 15 November 2014, case L 20119/KSBR at the Regional Court in Brno. Legal form spolek (registered association).
caveat: NOT A COMPANY but a registered nonprofit association, founded by Lukas Bryksa. SCOPE: a consumer cognitive-training site with about 25 online games for memory, attention and spatial orientation — brain-training software with no neural recording or stimulation.

name: Neomento
evidence: DZNE, the parent research centre: "Thus, based on knowledge from his research group, which is located at DZNE's Magdeburg site, neomento was founded in 2020."
caveat: The company's own site says the PROJECT was established in 2017 at DZNE and Charite — that is the research project, and 2020 is neomento GmbH. Co-founded by Prof. Thomas Wolbers. In scope: VR exposure therapy for social phobia, a certified Class I medical device.

name: Brainpaint
evidence: "Cora is President of BrainPaint, which she co-founded with Bill Scott in January of 2007."
caveat: The "our story" page carries a 2007-2019 copyright range which was NOT used; the January 2007 co-founding statement is independent of it. brainpaint.com is live and genuinely serves BrainPaint, an evidence-based EEG biofeedback system. Some listings say Los Angeles rather than Crystal Bay.

name: Monclarity
evidence: Aggregator profiles state Monclarity was founded in 2012 by Anatoly Tikhman with neuropsychologist Dr Elkhonon Goldberg.
caveat: Crunchbase returned 403 so even the aggregator record was not read directly, and no primary source states a year. The row is named Monclarity but points at brainwell.com: Monclarity LLC is the company and Brainwell its cognitive-training app. Brainwell launched October 2015 with a $5M Access Industries seed — a launch and funding date, not a founding.

name: Jogo Health
evidence: Reg CF offering detail: "Neural Therapeutics Inc was incorporated in the State of Delaware in June 2010. The company was renamed Jogohealth Inc. in 2016."
conflict: PitchBook lists 2010 and Tracxn 2016; the split is explained by the rename rather than two companies. The 2010 date is explicitly incorporation.

name: Halo Neuroscience
evidence: "Unlike most startups, Chao said the company didn't have a specific product in mind when it launched in 2013." Founders Daniel Chao and Brett Wingeier.
caveat: DEFUNCT: Halo Sport tDCS headphones for motor-cortex stimulation in athletic training; the company shut down and Flow Neuroscience acquired its assets, announced February 2021. Some aggregators add Amol Sarva and Lee Kraus to the founder list, which looks like contamination from a different Halo.

name: Forbrain
evidence: "Sound for Life was founded in 2014 by the owners of the Tomatis Method, the world-leader in auditory stimulation, to develop and market innovative, easy to use, and affordable brain stimulation products."
conflict: RocketReach says 2012 with founders Gregoire Tomatis and Thierry Gaujarengues, and Wikipedia dates the Forbrain DEVICE to 2010, which would predate both company dates and suggests the product existed under the Tomatis umbrella before Sound For Life Ltd was constituted.

name: MDDT inc
evidence: Tracxn lists 2013 for Movement Disorders Diagnostic Technologies Inc., London Ontario.
conflict: Not about the year alone: this row and "Movement Disorders Diagnostic Technologies (MDDT)" are the same entity and should be merged. Crunchbase's only hard date is a $50K grant round on 11 June 2013 — the aggregator founding year being IDENTICAL to the first funding event suggests it was back-derived from that round rather than sourced.

name: CoachAi
evidence: Crunchbase, Tracxn and PitchBook describe CoachAi as founded in 2016 by Nadav Sela, Shai Neiger and Daniel Cohen.
caveat: Aggregator-only; Startup Nation Finder and coachai.com both returned 403 so the live site is unverified. SCOPE: a gym and fitness-club member-retention app — an AI virtual personal trainer using behavioural economics to reduce churn. No sensing or physiological measurement of any kind.

name: Chestnut Medical
evidence: Crunchbase and PitchBook both give 2000 for Chestnut Medical, Menlo Park, founder Aaron L. Berez.
caveat: Aggregator-only: both ev3 press releases and two Berez biographies cite only the sale, never a founding year. In scope: the Pipeline Embolization Device for intracranial aneurysms, FDA PMA April 2011. ACQUIRED by ev3 — agreement announced 2 June 2009 and closed 24 June 2009, $75M upfront — then ev3 to Covidien in 2010 and Covidien to Medtronic in 2015.

name: Playlab London
evidence: Companies House: PLAYLAB LONDON LTD., company 08049362, incorporated 27 April 2012; DISSOLVED 10 March 2026. SIC 62020.
caveat: An incorporation date, though PitchBook and Crunchbase agree. The flagship product Flowy is a breathing-retraining puzzle game for panic attacks developed by founding director Simon Fox after his own panic attacks — mental-health games with guided breathing as a mechanic, no sensing. playlablondon.com fails its TLS handshake.

name: NeuroLeap
evidence: Inc42 company page: "Founded in 2017"; legal entity named as ADITRI NEUROSCIENCE PRIVATE LIMITED. Crunchbase, Tracxn and YourStory concur, founder Kumaar Bagrodia.
caveat: Genuinely in scope with real sensing: EEG-based non-invasive brain assessment and neurofeedback, incubated at IIT Palakkad. The legal name is Aditri Neuroscience Private Limited and "NeuroLeap" is the brand, so the Indian MCA register under that name is the authoritative source. Its only disclosed round is an angel round in August 2019, which is not the founding.

name: Lucine
evidence: French register: LUCINE SAS, SIREN 828 117 028, Bordeaux, date de creation 06/03/2017. Press reports of founding in Bordeaux in 2017 by Maryne Cotty-Eslous match exactly.
caveat: DEAD, and the domain is worse than dead. Judicial liquidation opened 5 July 2023, closed for insufficient assets 15 December 2025, struck off 16 December 2025, with the Endocare product sold to Butterfly Therapeutics. lucine.io has been RESOLD to an unrelated Telegram knowledge-management bot business that KEPT THE NAME and carries a "© 2026 Lucine" footer — the most misleading resold domain found in this sweep.

name: ThriveStreams
evidence: Crunchbase and Tracxn: founded 2012 in Brooklyn by Ryan Bruce Badilla and Adrian Cunanan; now marked deadpooled.
caveat: The founders' own post-mortem gives only that they "launched our iOS app in October 2014 and officially closed shop in August 2016" and describes the origin as a passion project, so 2012 is consistent with but not confirmed by the primary account. SHUT DOWN August 2016. SCOPE: a self-reported mood and symptom tracker with passive smartphone sensing — behavioural, not neural.

name: Open Ephys
evidence: "Since Open Ephys was founded in 2014, we've made it possible to build an entire extracellular electrophysiology rig from off-the-shelf open-source components."
conflict: Two different things with two different years: the open-source PROJECT began around 2010 in Matt Wilson's lab at MIT with Josh Siegle and Jakob Voigts, while the employee-owned COOPERATIVE dates to 2014. 2010 must not be attached to a company, because in 2010 there was no company.

name: Mensia Technologies
evidence: French RCS, SIREN 789458163: date de creation 01/11/2012. INRIA and trade press describe it as an INRIA spin-off created in October 2012.
caveat: DEAD: redressement judiciaire 29 May 2019, liquidation 25 July 2019, total asset sale to SAS myBrain Technologies effective 1 August 2019, liquidation closed 6 September 2021, struck off 9 September 2021. A genuine INRIA Rennes spin-off, EEG neurofeedback for ADHD on the NeuroRT platform built over OpenViBE. LOCATION: the registered seat was Chantepie near Rennes, not Paris.

name: Neural Sense
evidence: "Neural Sense was founded in 2010, but it's only with the explosion of neuromarketing accross Europe, America and Australia over the last few years that the company has really come to the forefront."
caveat: The company's own site states no founding year. An aggregator claim that co-founder Mark Drummond's role began November 2014 is a role start, not a competing founding. SCOPE: a neuromarketing consultancy that BUYS EEG, eye-tracking and biometric kit and sells advertising testing and shopper research — a measurement customer, not a developer.

name: Zenze
evidence: Danish CVR: ZenzeTech ApS, CVR 41657219, start date 1 September 2020, Diplomvej 381, Kongens Lyngby, industry manufacture of medical and dental instruments.
caveat: The real name is ZenzeTech ApS. BANKRUPT as of 22 December 2023 — the founders stated publicly they failed to close their investment round — confirmed by notice in Statstidende, and zenzetech.com is now a parked GoDaddy for-sale page. A DTU spin-out building a digital insole for continuous home gait monitoring in chronic neurological disease.

name: Yutai Intelligent
evidence: Profile for Xi'an Yutai Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., founded 2018, describing BCI medical industrialisation — brain-controlled interaction, VR/AR and rehabilitation robot systems — incubated by Xi'an Jiaotong University.
caveat: A single aggregator with no primary corroboration; no Chinese company-register record, XJTU announcement or Chinese-language news could be found. LOCATION: Xi'an, Shaanxi, which the index records only as "China" — and note the same aggregator says "Xi'an, Hunan", which is simply wrong and a reason to distrust its other fields. The missing website is consistent with a small domestic firm operating via WeChat and B2B portals.

name: Selfit Medical
evidence: Founded January 2017, Tel Aviv, AI-based digital therapy for the aging population; CB Insights carries the same year.
caveat: Verified independently as to business by Sheffield Hallam University's Advanced Wellbeing Research Centre accelerator, which took Selfit Medical Ltd as its first international startup — but that page states no founding year. In scope: a robot therapist projecting movement directions onto the floor with audio prompts, filming and reviewing the session for neuro-rehabilitation.

name: Avertus
evidence: PitchBook: Avertus founded 2012, Toronto — a cloud-supported neuromonitoring platform for real-time biomarker detection and personalised neuromodulation. CB Insights carries the same year.
caveat: avertus.ca does not resolve at all, a strong signal the company is defunct or dormant. Founded by Drs Peter Carlen and Berj Bardakjian of University of Toronto and Krembil, developing a wearable EEG headset monitoring ten brain areas for seizure control; an EpLink and Ontario Brain Institute portfolio company with research updates in 2016-17 and traces going quiet after about 2018. No primary source for the year.

name: KM Medical Software
evidence: Irish Times: "The Cork-based company was founded by Karuppiah Mahalingam, a consultant orthopaedic surgeon at Mater Private Hospital, in 2007."
conflict: A separate account says Mahalingam and his wife Mary "started the business in Cork in 2005". If the business began informally in 2005 then under a strict definition 2005 is the founding and 2007 merely incorporation, which would make the recorded year the wrong one of the two. An Irish CRO filing would settle it.

name: Nordic Neurostim
evidence: Danish CVR: Nordic-Neurostim ApS, CVR 38049909, start date 28 September 2016, status Normal.
conflict: Crunchbase, PitchBook and Dealroom all say 2013 against the register's 2016. The registry is favoured because the CVR number itself corroborates it: numbers are issued roughly sequentially and the 38-prefix block corresponds to 2016-17, so the record and the identifier agree. The 2013 claim may reflect a predecessor entity or the AAU project start.

name: Neurofenix
evidence: "Their meeting at Imperial College London in 2016 marked the birth of Neurofenix" — founders Guillem Singla Buxarais and Dimitrios Athanassiou.
caveat: In scope: the sensor-based NeuroBall platform for upper-limb rehabilitation after stroke, TBI and spinal cord injury. London and Atlanta. The $7M Series A in 2022 is a funding round, not the founding.

name: Quan Emerteq
evidence: PitchBook and Crunchbase both give 1998, Blaine, Minnesota. No primary source states the year.
caveat: ACQUIRED by Greatbatch Inc. for about $55M, announced 30 October 2007; Greatbatch is now Integer Holdings — which is why the index has no website. LOCATION: Blaine, MINNESOTA, which the index misspells as "Blain". SCOPE: a contract manufacturer of vascular catheters and CRM and neurostimulation lead components — a component supplier serving the neurostim market.

name: Contract Medical International
evidence: Company boilerplate reproduced in supplier directories: "Since its founding in late 2000, CMI has been providing... contract Manufacturing and R&D services to the medical device industry."
conflict: The German Handelsregister shows the Dresden GmbH, HRB 19782, first registered 24 November 2004 against the company's own claim of late 2000. Most likely the business began in 2000 — a Czech entity appears in the register as the GmbH's original shareholder — and the German GmbH was incorporated later. contract-medical.com has an expired TLS certificate so the company's own history page could not be read.

name: NEURONIX
evidence: Tracxn: founded 2008, Yokneam Illit, by Dr Jonathan Bentwich, who invented the platform after using it on his mother, an Alzheimer's patient. Crunchbase and PitchBook concur.
caveat: DEFUNCT. The neuroAD system interlaced rTMS with cognitive training and was CE-marked in 2012, but the FDA Neurological Devices Advisory Committee rejected it on efficacy in February 2019 after the pivotal trial of 131 patients missed its ADAS-Cog primary endpoint, and the company wound down. neuronixmedical.com no longer serves valid HTTPS. A UK "NEURONIX MEDICAL LTD" at Companies House is a later subsidiary whose date must not be borrowed.

name: Motorika
evidence: "Motorika was founded in 2004 by Professor Shlomo Ben Haim, a medical technology entrepreneur." Corroborated across PitchBook, CB Insights and LeadIQ; NASA Spinoff confirms Ben-Haim as founder but gives no year.
caveat: LOCATION: an Israeli company, Motorika Medical Ltd of Caesarea Industrial Park; Mount Laurel is the US subsidiary address, which several aggregators wrongly report as HQ. motorika.com is now a parked GoDaddy for-sale page, so no primary source survives and the company has probably wound down or restructured. In scope: ReoGo and ReoAmbulator neuro-rehabilitation robots.

name: Neurolite
evidence: "Neurolite was founded in 2011 by 4 partners sharing a strong determination to propose high-quality products from leading manufacturers to our customers." The Swiss commercial register independently gives 19.07.2011.
caveat: SCOPE: a distributor and authorised representative, not a manufacturer or developer — it resells third-party neurology, sleep-medicine and brain-stimulation systems into the Swiss market and does training and repairs. Belp with a Zurich subsidiary, about 14 employees.

name: Traumec Health Technology
evidence: "Traumec was born in Rio Claro, national orthopedic center in BRAZIL on 07/07/2007" — founded by three childhood friends from the metal-mechanic and polymer industry.
caveat: SCOPE: primarily an orthopaedic implant manufacturer whose portfolio spans cranio-maxillo-facial, extremities, neurosurgery and spine — cranial fixation plates and locking systems. Neuro-adjacent structural hardware rather than neural interfacing or neuromodulation.

name: Virtual Expert Clinics
evidence: Tracxn: founded 2004, Fredericton, with a Denver office; founder Cynthia Howroyd, a speech pathologist.
caveat: Aggregator-only; the earliest verifiable datum is the AutismPro launch release of 30 October 2006, a product launch. DEADPOOLED and autismpro.com refuses connections. SCOPE: AutismPro was a $69-89 monthly online subscription helping parents and teachers plan educational therapy programmes — curriculum and case-management software with no device or signal acquisition.

name: Niraxx Light Therapeutics, Inc.
evidence: Orange County Business Journal: "Nature Bright made light therapy devices for researchers... until 2016 when it newly launched as Niraxx." Paolo Cassano's biography states he co-founded Niraxx Light Therapeutics Inc. in November 2016.
conflict: Two 2016 accounts describing different events: OCBJ frames 2016 as a relaunch and rebrand of an existing company, Nature Bright, which would put the true founding earlier; the Cassano biography frames November 2016 as an original co-founding. Both land on 2016 for different reasons.

name: Nanobiosym
evidence: Lemelson-MIT: "In 2004, she founded Nanobiosym Labs as a research organization to develop her theories on how molecular motors work and Nanobiosym Diagnostics to create technologies to take advantage of her findings."
caveat: SCOPE: Anita Goel's nanobiophysics research institute plus a diagnostics spin-out, whose flagship Gene-RADAR is a mobile nucleic-acid platform for HIV, Ebola, TB and COVID. No nervous-system technology at all. The row does not say which of the two 2004 entities it means; nanobiosym.com is live but stale with a 2019 copyright and a 404 about page.

name: Progressive Nuero
evidence: "Zeller and Follmer laid the stepping stone of Progressive NEURO, Inc. in 2018."
caveat: The index name is MISSPELLED: the company is Progressive NEURO, Inc. Crunchbase carries the identical typo, which suggests the row was seeded from there. In scope: ischaemic-stroke neurothrombectomy devices, founders Kirk Zeller and Brett Follmer. LOCATION: aggregators say Santa Clara but the company's own site lists Ravenna, Nebraska, where it was incubated at Zeller's Silicon Prairie Center.

name: Saccadous
evidence: "Saccadous was founded in 2014 on the hypothesis that eye movements of people with neurological disorders differ from healthy age-matched controls."
caveat: In scope: microsaccade and eye-movement analysis for diagnosis and tracking of Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and TBI. Founded and initially funded January 2014 via the ASU Furnace technology-transfer accelerator, consistent with the stated year.

name: Medicortex Finland Oy
evidence: "Medicortex was founded by Dr. Adrian Harel in Turku in 2014."
caveat: SCOPE: a diagnostics company rather than a device maker — a glycan-biomarker point-of-care test detecting traumatic brain injury from saliva or urine, with a secondary therapeutics ambition. The entity is now Medicortex Finland Oyj, a public limited company, and search results indicate NOSIUM acquired a majority stake in November 2025, unverified against a primary source.

name: Anaconda BioMed
evidence: "Anaconda Biomed was founded in 2015" — by Dr Ofir Arad and Dr Marc Ribo, a neurologist at Hospital Vall d'Hebron, Barcelona.
caveat: From the EU's EIC Scaling Club, an institutional programme page. In scope: the ANA funnel catheter, a mechanical thrombectomy system for acute ischaemic stroke. The company's own homepage confirms the entity but states no year and /about-us/ 404s. SOLONDA first-in-human data published in Stroke April 2022; CE Mark for ANA5 June 2025.

name: TherapyCharts
evidence: Tracxn, CB Insights and Crunchbase all give 2008, Ann Arbor, founders Ryan Dibble and Lisa Farmer.
caveat: Aggregator-only. The company's own site shows a "2008-2026" copyright RANGE, which was not counted, though it is consistent. Local journalism from 2010 confirms Lisa Farmer founded it after working in hospital mental health but gives no year. SCOPE: a HIPAA-compliant web EHR with treatment planning, notes and billing for psychologists and counsellors — records software for talk-therapy practices.

name: CVAid Medical
evidence: "CVAid was established in 2018 by a group of entrepreneurs who combine business, tech and medical expertise."
caveat: Company-issued boilerplate matching aggregator records. AI tele-stroke triage, Tel Aviv. The year is not back-derived: the $4M Series A came in 2022, four years later.

name: Theranica
evidence: "Theranica is a medical device company, founded in 2016 by Alon Ironi, Ronen Jashek, Rotislav (Slava) Barabash and Dr. Shimon Eckhouse."
caveat: A loose 2015 circulates in search summaries but could not be traced to any source; the company's own boilerplate says 2016. Legal name Theranica Bio-Electronics Ltd; Nerivio is FDA-cleared remote electrical neuromodulation for migraine.

name: e(ye)BRAIN
evidence: French register, SIREN 502400419: creation 5 February 2008; "Radiée le 17 janvier 2018".
caveat: DEAD. Safeguard 5 August 2015, judicial reorganisation 18 November 2015, LIQUIDATION 20 January 2016, struck off 17 January 2018. Founded by Serge Kinkingnehun at Ivry-sur-Seine. The EyeBrain technology was acquired by SuriCog in 2016, and SuriCog's own 2013 founding must not migrate onto this row. Distinct from eyeBrain Medical of Texas.

name: CardiaCare
evidence: Tracxn gives January 2015, founders Amos Ziv and Tsahi Holand.
caveat: Aggregator-only; the company site has no history page. SCOPE survives the check despite the name: its own site describes "Median-Vagus modulation (mVNS)" and states that neuromodulation of the median and ulnar nerves of the wrist reaches the brain — a closed-loop peripheral neuromodulation wearable for atrial fibrillation. Not funding-back-derived; first funding was around 2023.

name: PGV
evidence: Company profile: 設立：2016年9月16日 — established 16 September 2016. Corroborated by NIKKEI COMPASS and JST's COI venture listing.
caveat: An Osaka University-derived venture despite the Tokyo HQ. Ultra-thin patch-type EEG electrodes with Japanese Class II medical device certification, plus automatic sleep-stage scoring. The name derives from "Perpetual Gratitude & Voyage".

name: OccamzRazor
evidence: "The company was founded in 2015 by German medical researcher Katharina Sophia Volz."
caveat: Corroborated by Crunchbase, PitchBook and Tracxn but no company-site or institutional statement exists, and the supporting source is a low-tier biotech blog. An AI knowledge-graph for Parkinson's; still operating but shrunk from about 17 employees in 2022 to 7 in 2026.

name: EndoRon Medical
evidence: Israeli register: ENDORON MEDICAL LTD, registration 516049129, incorporation 1 July 2019, status active, Kfar Saba.
caveat: An incorporation date, though aggregators independently give 2019 and a September 2019 launch. SCOPE: an endovascular anchoring device for aortic EVAR and cardiovascular treatment. Not neurotechnology.

name: Tingles
evidence: Aggregators give 2017; Y Combinator Winter 2018 batch, accepted October 2017.
caveat: TechCrunch of 16 March 2018 says only "In the year since... co-founders launched" — a relative phrase that was not converted, which is why this rests on aggregators alone. SCOPE: an ASMR video and audio relaxation app. LOCATION: Newark, DELAWARE, a registered-agent address rather than an operating base; the founders are Slovenian.

name: Neurophony
evidence: "Founded in 2020 by Ria Rustagi and Bhavya Madan, Neuphony leverages advanced EEG technology."
caveat: Two index errors: the name is Neuphony, not Neurophony, and the company is INDIAN, headquartered in Delhi NCR — the Munich location is wrong. It appeared on Shark Tank India. Tracxn flags it as no longer operational around October 2024 while neuphony.com still markets the headband; that contradiction is unresolved.

name: National Seating & Mobility
evidence: Company boilerplate: "Founded in 1992, the company has grown from five locations to a national network of professional Assistive Technology Providers."
caveat: The NSM about page says only "For more than 30 years", a relative phrase that was not used. SCOPE: a durable medical equipment distributor and service network — custom wheelchairs, seating, stair and vehicle lifts, ramps, repairs. A retailer and installer, not a developer.

name: NEOS Surgery
evidence: "NEOS Surgery was born in October 2003 as a micro-SME that combined the efforts of neurosurgeons with two Technology Centres."
caveat: A research-institute spin-off combining neurosurgeons with EURECAT of Barcelona and TECNALIA of San Sebastian. Products Cranial LOOP and Cranial COVER for cranial bone-flap fixation, plus STERN FIX for sternal closure — neurosurgical hardware rather than a neural interface, and one line is cardiothoracic.

name: Boston Scientific Neuromodulation Corporation
evidence: Boston Scientific release of 1 June 2004: "Advanced Bionics was founded in 1993 by Al Mann to develop and manufacture cochlear implants for profoundly deaf children and adults."
conflict: Three years belong to three different things and must not be blended. 1993 is Advanced Bionics' founding and the direct ancestor of this Valencia entity. 2004 is Boston Scientific's acquisition. 2008 is the restructuring that kept the neurostimulation business and renamed it Boston Scientific Neuromodulation, while the cochlear business went back toward Mann and later to Sonova. 1979 is Boston Scientific Corporation's own founding and belongs to the separate row.

name: Fatigue Science
evidence: BC Tech Association: "Fatigue Science was founded in 2006 in Vancouver, with the purpose of creating safer work environments for workers in the mining industry."
caveat: An industry association rather than an aggregator. Founded by Pat Byrne, who acquired rights to the US Army-derived SAFTE biomathematical fatigue algorithm. Repositioned from the ReadiBand wearable to the Readi platform — a product change, not a rename. SCOPE: actigraphy plus a cognitive-effectiveness model, with no direct neural sensing.

name: QMENTA
evidence: About page: the founders "decided in 2013 to build the infrastructure they'd needed themselves, regulated and cloud-native from day one." Corroborated by "Created in 2013 in Boston and Barcelona."
caveat: Originally named MINT LABS — CB Insights still resolves the profile at /company/mint-labs and QMENTA's own page says Rodrigues "Co-founded Mint Labs". A rebrand, not a new founding. Founders Vesna Prchkovska and Paulo Rodrigues; dual HQ Boston and Barcelona.

name: HoloSurgical
evidence: "It was founded in 2015 by virtual and augmented reality expert Prof. Cristian Luciano, PhD, and spine surgeon Dr. Kris Siemionow, MD, PhD, and in 2016 joined by Prof. Paul Lewicki, PhD."
caveat: The legal entity is Holo Surgical Inc.; "HoloSurgical" is the brand. ACQUIRED by Surgalign Holdings, announced 29 September 2020 and closed 23 October 2020 for up to $125M, so it has not been independent since. ARAI is augmented-reality and AI spine surgery navigation.

name: Ten Percent Happier
evidence: Boston.com, 22 January 2014: "The pair began working together last January, initially under the name Revv" — that is January 2013. Founders Ben Rubin and Derek Haswell, both ex-Zeo.
conflict: The company's own current story page starts at 2014 and marks 2015 as the Ten Percent Happier relaunch. Dating the entity gives 2013; dating the brand gives 2015. The chain is Revv (Jan 2013) to Change Collective (Jan 2014) to Ten Percent Happier (2015) to Happier Meditation (2024), and Dan Harris left on 1 March 2025 taking the podcast.

name: Kadho
evidence: TechCrunch: "Kadho has been around since 2014", founded by PhDs with AI and neuroscience backgrounds, Kaveh Azartash and Dhonam Pemba.
caveat: kadho.com now redirects to HugeDomains — parked and for sale. The product line moved to KidSense.ai and Crunchbase files the org under KidSense; a Kadho Sports arm also exists. The name is an acronym of the founders' first names. SCOPE: children's speech recognition and language learning with a neuroplasticity marketing story.

name: RYKLIN SOFTWARE
evidence: New York register: RYKLIN SOFTWARE, INC. established 18 December 2001 as a domestic business corporation, Brooklyn; status Inactive, "dissolution date is Sep 30 2023".
caveat: An incorporation date. DISSOLVED 30 September 2023. ryklinsoftware.com now serves Neuro-Software Developers, Inc. — contract software for eye tracking, gaze analysis and neuro-electrophysiology — which reads as a SUCCESSOR entity by the same person, Edward Ryklin of the Burke Neurological Institute, rather than a resale to a stranger. The succession was not verified against a register.

name: Cerebro Medical Systems
evidence: Company boilerplate: "Founded in 2010 and based in Pleasanton, CA", a VC-backed company designing neurotechnology for brain-injured patients.
conflict: Not about the year: there is no company called "Cerebro Medical Systems". The entity is Cerebrotech Medical Systems, which is the OTHER row in this index at the same domain and address. This row is both a duplicate and misnamed.

name: Voicery
evidence: Y Combinator profile: founded 2017, batch Winter 2018, status Inactive; founder Andrew Gibiansky, previously leader of the speech synthesis research team at Baidu Research.
caveat: NO ACQUISITION could be found by any acquirer across three searches, contrary to the briefing: YC marks the company Inactive and the platform was discontinued in 2020, which reads as a shutdown rather than an exit. Sources disagree on the founder, some naming Bobby Ullman. SCOPE: "neural" here means deep neural networks for speech synthesis, with no connection to the nervous system.

name: Headsafe
evidence: "Headsafe was established in Sydney, Australia, in 2017 by Dr. Adrian Cohen to develop and commercialise the patented NUROCHEK system."
conflict: A separate "HeadSafe" was established in 1987 as the concussion programme of Necksafe Ltd, an Australian not-for-profit also associated with Dr Adrian Cohen — so the NAME predates the company by thirty years. 2017 is the commercial MedTech entity that built NUROCHEK; 1987 is a nonprofit programme.

name: Perceiv AI
evidence: Mila: "Founded in 2018, Perceiv AI is a precision medicine technology company dedicated to improving treatment efficacy through refined patients selection", "Founded by graduate students out of University of Montreal and Mila" — Christian Dansereau and Cesar Laurent.
caveat: Mila hosts the lab the founders came from, so this is close to primary. SCOPE: AI prognostic biomarkers for clinical-trial patient selection, Alzheimer's first — analytics rather than a device or interface.

name: Eye Predict
evidence: SBIR company record for Eye-Predict LLC: "Year Founded: 2008", Los Angeles, president Ran Carmi; first SBIR award year 2010.
caveat: An SBIR-data aggregator whose company records derive from SBA registration data, so better than a generic aggregator, but no primary source confirms it. The 2008 year differs from the first award year of 2010, so it is not obviously back-derived. The current product is MindFind, a visuotactile assessment battery for monitoring mental functioning after brain injury.

name: Plexon Neuroscience
evidence: "Founded in 1983 in Dallas, Texas by Harvey Wiggins, Plexon (under the initial name of Spectrum Scientific) has grown from a one-person shop to a full team of innovative engineers, biophysicists and neuroscientists."
caveat: Corroborated by a 2013 Neurotech Reports profile marking its 30th anniversary. Founded under the name SPECTRUM SCIENTIFIC, so 1983 is the predecessor that became Plexon. The legal name is Plexon Inc, not "Plexon Neuroscience". Multichannel electrophysiology and OmniPlex data acquisition — squarely in scope.

name: Evasc
evidence: CB Insights: "Founded Year: 2001." Vancouver.
caveat: Aggregator-grade: evasc.com/about and the CEO bio both call Dr Donald Ricci a co-founder but give no year, and the site footer shows 2026, which was not used. Now trades as Evasc Neurovascular Enterprises; the eCLIPs bifurcation flow diverter is still shipping with 2025 registry data across 280+ patients. Not obviously funding-back-derived. A BC registry lookup would settle it.

name: SyncVR
evidence: The Hub startup profile lists founded 2018 for SyncVR Medical, Utrecht, founded by Robbert Brouwer with Evan van der Holst, Floris van der Breggen and Freek van Polen.
caveat: The company's own about pages redirect to a US subdomain that returns empty content, so this rests on startup directories. A VR and XR platform for pain and anxiety reduction and clinical training across 125+ institutions. NOTE: Invest in Denmark says "In 2021, the Dutch start-up company, SyncVR Medical, established a Nordic headquarter in Denmark" — a market expansion, and The Hub itself wrongly lists Denmark as HQ. The company is Dutch.

name: Cognision
evidence: "John H. Barker, MD and Kalford C. Fadem founded Neuronetrix in 2003."
caveat: The legal entity is Neuronetrix Solutions, LLC, dba COGNISION — so the row is named after the brand. The FDA-cleared COGNISION EEG and ERP headset for cognitive assessment in dementia and schizophrenia trials. Genuinely distinct from Cognionics.

name: Aleva Neurotherapeutics
evidence: EPFL: "Aleva was established in 2008 on the basis of doctoral research carried out by Andre Mercanzini, now the firm's CTO."
caveat: An EPFL spin-off from the Renaud Microsystems Lab; directSTIM directional deep brain stimulation leads, CE marked December 2019. The website is degraded — both the root and /about return 404 — and combined with known financial difficulty the operating status is questionable, though no Swiss dissolution was confirmed.

name: Stroke Rehab
evidence: A company-issued Series A release and Startup Nation Central both give establishment in 2012; the device is Stimel-03.
caveat: The legal entity is MOTION INFORMATICS LTD, Israeli company 514816222, Haifa — "Stroke Rehab" is the trading name, so the row is on the brand. Stimel-03 combines biofeedback with FES and NMES for post-stroke motor recovery. A US distribution partnership with ReShape Lifesciences was signed April 2025 and registry activity runs through mid-2026, so it appears live. cvarehab.com refused connections.

name: Guanhao Biotech
evidence: Founded 1999, Guangzhou; "develops, manufactures, and sells regenerative medicines and life sciences products in China." Yahoo Finance agrees.
caveat: From financial-data profiles rather than filings. SCOPE: Guangdong Guanhao Biotech (Shenzhen-listed, 300238) is a regenerative BIOMATERIALS manufacturer — dura repair patches, wound dressings, corneal grafts. Dural patches are used in neurosurgery, which is presumably why it was swept in, but that is materials science. It is also a large public company, far outside the profile of the rest of the index.

name: Neuro Device Group
evidence: Polish KRS 0000318277: "Data założenia: 2008" — the company "rozpoczęła działalność w 2008 roku".
caveat: Two caveats. The 2008 start was in market research and PR, not medical devices; the company pivoted to neurotech later, so 2008 is the legal entity rather than the neurotech business. And an entity cluster needs untangling: alongside Neuro Device Group Sp. z o.o. the KRS shows Neuro Device Sp. z o.o. w likwidacji and Neuro Device Lab Sp. z o.o. w likwidacji, plus a Neuro Device S.A. The site's TLS certificate is misconfigured.

name: Encora
evidence: "Encora traces its origins to an MIT spinout founded in 2019, built around wrist-based stimulation for tremor relief."
conflict: Crunchbase says 2018 against 2019 in sourced reporting, and which marks founding versus incorporation is unresolved.

name: Conscious Labs
evidence: CONSCIOUS LABS SAS, SIREN 812702744, date de création 24 juillet 2015.
conflict: CB Insights and other aggregators say 2014 against the register's 2015. The register date is incorporation, so an informal 2014 founding is possible, but 2014 is unsourced and may be back-derived.

name: Virtuleap
evidence: CB Insights: "Founded Year: 2018", corroborated by Crunchbase, PitchBook and Preqin all giving January 2018, and by press describing a January 2018 start in Portugal with a pivot to VR brain training in May 2019.
caveat: No primary source: virtuleap.com is JS-rendered and returns no text, and directories returned 403 or 522. The founders ran VR hackathon activity under the Virtuleap name as early as 2016-17, so an earlier informal origin is plausible but unsourced. Product Enhance VR, cognitive training and assessment.

name: Afferent Technologies
evidence: The Catalan government ACCIO startup directory lists AFFERENT TECHNOLOGIES SL as founded 2016, at the UAB Research Park, flagged as a university spinoff.
caveat: A government directory rather than a commercial aggregator, but still a directory. LOCATION: Cerdanyola del Valles at the UAB Research Park rather than Barcelona city. SCOPE DRIFT: its own site now presents the business as a tech incubator plus a funding-advisory arm writing EU grant proposals, alongside the WiNerve intraoperative neuromonitoring instrumentation. Do not confuse with Afferent Medical Solutions or Afference.

name: Machine Medicine
evidence: Companies House: MACHINE MEDICINE TECHNOLOGIES LIMITED, company 10787420, incorporated 24 May 2017, status Active.
caveat: An incorporation date, but multiple independent write-ups also say 2017. STILL TRADING — accounts filed to 31 October 2025 and a confirmation statement dated 7 March 2026, nothing overdue, no previous names. machinemedicine.com now redirects to machinemedicine.io. Beware a decoy: a separate MACHINE MEDICINE LIMITED (09023886) was dissolved 31 October 2017 and is a different entity.

name: AudioCardio
evidence: LA Business Journal: "Ellis' app is the centerpiece of Santa Monica hearing therapy company AudioCardio Inc., which he co-founded in 2018 with a scientist from South Korea named Sam Kwok."
caveat: The Santa Monica Daily Press says only that the app "launched about five years ago", a relative phrase that was not converted. SCOPE: threshold sound therapy for hearing loss and tinnitus — audiology, where the claimed mechanism is cochlear rather than neuromodulation.

name: Rapid Medical
evidence: "Founded in 2008 by CEO Ronen Eckhouse and Chairman of the Board Shimon Eckhouse, Rapid Medical is seeking to further commercialize..."
caveat: Father-and-son founders; Shimon Eckhouse also co-founded Lumenis. TIGERTRIEVER, the first adjustable stent retriever, FDA-cleared March 2021, plus COMANECI and DRIVEWIRE. Squarely in scope. The company's own about page states no year.

name: EndoStream
evidence: "Founded in 2015 by Danel Mayer, CEO, and Alon May, VP of Technology, Endostream has developed an implant device called Nautilus for the treatment of brain aneurysms."
caveat: ACQUIRED by Kaneka Corporation of Japan, announced January 2025 at roughly a $100M valuation, so it is now a subsidiary. LOCATION: Or Akiva, not the Tel Aviv the index records. The Nautilus intrasaccular system for wide-neck intracranial aneurysms, CE marked November 2024.

name: customKYnetics
evidence: SBIR company profile: customKYnetics, Inc., Versailles, Kentucky, founded 2000, "a research and development company focused on the development of rehabilitation engineering products"; status recorded Inactive as of March 2017.
caveat: The "KY" is indeed Kentucky and the Versailles location is right. Corroborated as a real trading entity by 11 SBIR Phase I awards, 4 Phase II awards, Kentucky state matching grants and US patent 8271090B1. A University of Kentucky spinout, but note the ASTeCC incubator's "February 2003" is an incubator GRADUATION date, not a founding. No website exists; the stored "https://customKYnetics" is not a URL. Possibly dormant since about 2012.

name: Axem Neurotechnology
evidence: AXEM NEUROTECHNOLOGY INC., corporation 9822305, incorporated 7 July 2016 under the Canada Business Corporations Act, status Active, Dartmouth NS.
caveat: From a third-party mirror of Corporations Canada rather than the official register, though aggregators independently give 2016. A Dalhousie spinout from the Laboratory for Brain Recovery and Function; a portable wireless fNIRS headband, refocused from athlete training to post-stroke rehabilitation, with PLOS ONE validation and trial NCT05258591. Accelerator dates — CDL-Vancouver 2018/19, HAX Shenzhen 2018 — must not be mistaken for the founding. axemneuro.com fails DNS entirely.

name: Motognosis
evidence: Startbase: "Founding Year: 2014", corroborated by German startup press — "Motognosis wurde 2014 aus dem Labor der Charité Neurodiagnostik... gegründet", founders Sebastian Mansow-Model, Karen Otte and Dr Alexander Brandt.
caveat: motognosis.com serves an expired TLS certificate and motognosis.de refuses HTTPS, so no primary source was reachable. A Charite Berlin and NeuroCure spinout doing 3D-camera motion analysis for MS and Parkinson's. A January 2021 IBB Ventures round is widely reported and could be back-derived by some aggregators, but 2014 is not that date.

name: The Learning Corp
evidence: "Founded in 2013, the company is based on the research of Boston University professor Swathi Kiran."
conflict: Several profiles give 2012, which is likely when the underlying BU research and app work began — Constant Therapy was developed in Kiran's lab in 2012 and launched 2014 — while 2013 attaches to the incorporated business. Which the index should carry is unresolved.

name: SPEAK MODalities
evidence: Purdue newsroom: SPEAK MODalities LLC was formed in 2013, co-founded by Oliver Wendt, Michael Zentner and Diana Hancock.
conflict: Some summaries say 2014, very likely contaminated by two adjacent facts in the same release: the release is dated Q1 2014 and "the first commercially supported version of SPEAKall! was released in January of 2014", a product launch. Three distinct dates are easy to confuse here — a 2012 Purdue EPICS project, the 2013 company, the 2014 launch.

name: NeuroScouting
evidence: The company's own site states the founders "started NeuroScouting in 2007 with the mission of bringing the latest neuroscience advances out of the lab and into actionable tools in the real world."
caveat: From the company itself rather than an aggregator, consistent with SI and AP reporting naming founders Drs Wesley Clapp and Brian Miller. Still operating, with current job postings. LOCATION: Somerville, not the Cambridge the index records. Scope is broader than athlete cognitive training — it also runs a brain-health arm with NIH SBIR funding for executive-function deficits in concussion. The site's "2008-2025" footer range disagrees with the stated 2007 and was not used.

name: Techno Concept
evidence: French register, SIREN 420 025 454: date de création 01/08/1998, registered at the Manosque commercial court 07/09/1998, status active.
caveat: A registry creation date, which for a French SAS is effectively the founding, though an earlier legal form would not show. SAS, capital 576,900 euro, 20-49 employees, address matching the index exactly. technoconcept.fr failed on every attempt, so the EEG and evoked-potential business could not be confirmed from the company itself; the register classifies it under engineering and technical studies.

name: Saccade Diagnostics
evidence: Companies House: SACCADE DIAGNOSTICS LIMITED, SC475291, incorporated 14 April 2014; registered as LISTER SQUARE (NO 219) LIMITED until 5 June 2014, then renamed.
conflict: The registry date is a SHELF-COMPANY incorporation — the vehicle was Lister Square No 219 and only became Saccade on 5 June 2014 — so it says nothing about the venture. The University of Aberdeen reports the spinout winning first prizes in Converge Challenge and Best Open Innovation Business in 2013, before the vehicle existed. 2014 is the company, 2013 the venture.

name: Altoida
evidence: "Established in 2016 in Luzern, Altoida is a pioneer in brain health and digital biomarker science." Founders Ioannis Tarnanas, Richard Fischer and Maximilian Buegler.
caveat: Swiss in origin — Altoida AG of Lucerne — with a US entity, Altoida Inc., fronting the business later; the company page gives a Washington DC address, so the index matches current HQ but not the founding jurisdiction. In scope: an AR and tablet-based digital neuro-biomarker platform for Alzheimer's with FDA Breakthrough Device designation. The Swiss commercial register returned 403.

name: Special Minds
evidence: "Special Minds IT er etableret i 2004 - dengang under navnet BOAS Specialister - som nonprofit virksomhed. Vi er registreret socialøkonomisk virksomhed (RSV)."
caveat: RENAMED from BOAS Specialister. NOT A COMPANY in the ordinary sense: a registered social-economy enterprise and part of Den Sociale Udviklingsfond, a non-profit charitable foundation. LOCATION: DANISH, with departments in Aarhus, Aalborg, Silkeborg and Kolding — the index's Istanbul, Turkey is wrong. SCOPE: employing, training and placing autistic people in IT work such as accessibility testing. A sibling of the Specialisterne model but a distinct organisation.

name: Deneb Medical
evidence: Deneb Medical SL, NIF B75107649, Registro Mercantil registration 31 March 2014; directors Juan Arregui Altuna and Aritz Lazcoz del Campo.
caveat: A registration date with no separate founding statement found, though Dealroom and PitchBook independently say "launched March 2014". Active on recent 2025-26 filings, no name changes. SCOPE: the Izar surgical robotics platform serving neurosurgery, CMF, head and neck, urology and general surgery — surgical robotics where neurosurgery is one application among several.

name: Imagine Eyes
evidence: "Since he cofounded Imagine Eyes in 2003, he has established partnerships with scientific and clinical centers."
caveat: The year comes from a FOUNDER BIOGRAPHY on the company's own page — normally a refused source class — but it is the company's own statement about its own founding, internally consistent, with no competing year. SCOPE: the rtx1 adaptive-optics retinal camera imaging photoreceptors and retinal vasculature. The retina is CNS tissue and the technique appears in neurodegeneration research, but the company's market and regulatory positioning are ophthalmology.

name: Medical Guardian
evidence: Philadelphia Inquirer: the company launched in 2005 out of founder Geoff Gross’s Center City apartment.
caveat: SCOPE: personal emergency response systems — pendant and watch panic buttons with fall detection and 24/7 call-centre monitoring for seniors. No nervous-system technology of any kind. The company’s own about page says only "20 years", a relative phrase not used here.

name: Blckb
evidence: Blckb Applied Neuroscience Ltd, established February 2013 as a University of Ljubljana spin-off, founded by Luka Zevnik.
caveat: blckb.eu does not resolve (NXDOMAIN), so the company’s own about page could not be read; the February 2013 wording survives only in a search-engine cache and aggregator profiles. Aggregators place the registered company in Logatec, not Ljubljana.

name: Eodyne
evidence: "Eodyne Systems was established in 2014" as a spin-off of the SPECS research group at Universitat Pompeu Fabra.
caveat: The spin-off relationship is confirmed by UPF, ICREA and SOMMa, but none of those institutional pages states a year; 2014 is aggregator-sourced only. Eodyne and Eodyne Systems are one company — eodyne.com 302-redirects to eodynesystems.com.

name: Newronika
evidence: "In 2008, Alberto Priori founded Newronika SpA, a spin-off company of the University of Milan and Fondazione IRCCS Ca’ Granda."
conflict: Sources tied to founder Alberto Priori give 2008; FierceBiotech and CB Insights give 2016. 2016 is most likely the recapitalisation when Newronika became a venture-backed operating company, which is not a founding, but that provenance could not be proved.
caveat: The company’s own about page states no founding year, only "two decades of work", a relative phrase not used here.

name: Neuromod
evidence: "Founded in 2010, Neuromod Devices is a global medical technology business" — founded by Dr Ross O’Neill, headquartered in Dublin.

name: Phenox
evidence: "Since its founding in 2005, phenox has been dedicated to developing innovative, breakthrough and clinically proven technologies and solutions for the treatment of neurovascular diseases."
caveat: Wallaby Medical acquired phenox on 26 April 2022 and the entity now trades as WallabyPhenox; the 2005 year belongs to phenox GmbH of Bochum, not to Wallaby Medical.

name: Beats Medical
evidence: "Founded in 2012 by Ms Clancy, who launched the company when she was just 22 years old, Beats Medical has developed an app..."
caveat: A 2016 Irish Times interview quotes founder Ciara Clancy saying "We have been going for nearly three years"; that relative phrase was not computed from. 2012 is stated explicitly in several independent reports.

name: Vuno
evidence: "The company achieved many ‘firsts’ since its foundation in 2014..."
caveat: SCOPE: a general medical-imaging and clinical AI company (bone age, chest X-ray, fundus, lung CT, ECG). Brain MRI is one product line among many. KOSDAQ:338220, IPO February 2021.

name: Clinical Science Systems
evidence: KvK-derived record: established 12-02-2004, KvK number 27265075, Vennootschap onder firma, Leiden.
caveat: The KvK number and date are registry-derived but reached through a scraped directory that mis-categorises the company as web design; the company’s own site states no founding year.

name: CAIDE Systems
evidence: "The company, founded in 2016, is led by Kyewook ‘Jacob’ Lee who took Ph.D. courses in computer science at University of Massachusetts Lowell."
caveat: SCOPE: a general medical deep-learning imaging platform across X-ray, CT, MRI and ultrasound; its first model is brain stroke detection, which is what makes it neuro-adjacent.

name: Medicalcooling
evidence: Neue Westfälische: Medical Cooling founded 2012 in Gütersloh by Fabian Temme and Ruben Brühl.
caveat: PROVISIONAL. The article returned HTTP 423 Locked, so the year comes from the search index’s rendering of it rather than a direct read. The company originated as a research project at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg and its AIRCHILL platform is still described on its own site as a TRL-4 laboratory demonstrator. Not to be confused with EMCOOLS Medical Cooling Systems GmbH of Austria.

name: Netrin
evidence: Netrin Sports Technologies Private Limited, CIN U74999TG2019PTC135453, incorporated 16 September 2019, Registrar of Companies Hyderabad.
caveat: This is an INCORPORATION date, not a stated founding; the underlying physiological-monitoring research at IIT Madras predates it by about seven years. SCOPE: a sports and human-performance company (Conqur), with no neuro product. The CIN encodes Telangana, so the index’s Chennai location is doubtful.

name: Mila
evidence: "L’entreprise Mila a été créée en 2018."
caveat: From an accelerator profile rather than the company’s own site or a registry. This is the Paris École Polytechnique startup behind Mila-Learn, a CE-marked rhythm-game medical device for dyslexia — NOT Mila Quebec, the Montreal AI institute.

name: AddBrain Inc
evidence: Non-distributing corporation with 50 or fewer shareholders, 6020 Vine St Suite 322, Vancouver BC, registered 25 May 2018.
caveat: An INCORPORATION date, not a stated founding. addbrain.ca 301-redirects to brainheals.org, which carries AddBrain’s content but states no year.

name: Medtronic
evidence: On 29 April 1949 Earl Bakken and his brother-in-law Palmer Hermundslie formed a business partnership named Medtronic in a converted boxcar garage in Minneapolis; the first month’s revenue was eight dollars for repairing a centrifuge.
caveat: The index records medina-medical.com as this row’s website — Medina Medical was a neurovascular startup Medtronic ACQUIRED in 2015. The correct domain is medtronic.com. The index also holds separate "Medtronic Vascular" and "Medtronicdbs" rows.

name: AppliedVR
evidence: "Founded in 2015, AppliedVR is developing a digital health platform that utilizes therapeutic virtual reality to treat chronic- and acute-pain patients."
caveat: 2015 is the founding, not the 2016 Techstars Cedars-Sinai cohort. Spun out of market-research firm LRW by David Sackman, Matthew Stoudt and Josh Sackman.

name: Alpha Omega
evidence: Founded in 1993 as a small engineering office in Nazareth by Imad Younis, initially a sub-contractor in medical device design, later specialising in brain surgery products.
caveat: The index records "Guangzhou, China"; the company is headquartered in Nazareth Industrial Park, Israel. The China association is most likely back-derived from a Chinese joint venture, which is not a headquarters.

name: Vagustim
evidence: "Medical Doctor Ali Veysel Özden and Engineer Ali Can Erk joined forces in 2017 to develop the first prototype."
caveat: The about page never says "founded in". 2017 is a prototype milestone, the closest thing to a founding event stated; 2015 is idea-origin, 2018 a contest final and 2019 the first investment, none of which were used. The index records San Francisco; Vagustim is Turkish, at İTÜ AR I Teknokent, Istanbul.

name: Quincy Bioscience
evidence: "Quincy was founded in Madison in 2004 by Mark Underwood, Quincy’s president, and Michael Beaman, its chief executive officer."
caveat: SCOPE: a jellyfish-protein (apoaequorin) dietary supplement, Prevagen — no device, no neural interface. In 2017 the FTC and the New York Attorney General sued over advertising claims, alleging the Madison Memory Study failed to show a statistically significant improvement over placebo on any of nine cognitive tasks.

name: Perflow Medical
evidence: "The company was founded in 2014 in the RAD Biomed Incubator by CEO Danny Farin" — co-founders Dr Eyal Orion, Gilad Cibulski and Avi Rappaport.
conflict: PitchBook, Dealroom and CB Insights report 2010; Globes reports 2014 with named founders and a named incubator. The entity may have existed in the incubator from 2010 and been formally constituted in 2014.
caveat: Acquired by a Chinese private equity firm for about $100M, announced January 2022. Both perflow.com and perflowmedical.com present a certificate for vps50022.secured-cloud2.net, so no company-controlled page could be read.

name: Progeny Software
evidence: Mergr lists Progeny Software as established 1996 and acquired by Ambry Genetics Corp on 2015-04-01.
caveat: The only corroboration on the company’s own site is a footer copyright range, which is not a source. SCOPE: genetic pedigree drawing and hereditary cancer risk software, nothing nervous-system-specific; now an Ambry subsidiary trading as Progeny Genetics, LLC.

name: Thompson SCI
evidence: Gust profile: Thompson SCI, Salem, New Hampshire, "Founded: March 2012", medical devices, 4 employees.
caveat: A single self-reported startup profile is the only source carrying a year — no registry, news or company-site corroboration. thompsonsci.com fails its TLS handshake, so the company appears dormant. Salem is in New Hampshire, not Massachusetts or Oregon.

name: Guiding Technologies
evidence: inKnowVation SBIR record for Guiding Technologies Corporation, Philadelphia PA: "Founded: 2013"; first SBIR award 2015.
conflict: Several sources imply a 2014-2015 origin, the NSF SBIR Phase I having been awarded in January 2015. Neither the company’s own site nor Temple University nor Ben Franklin Technology Partners states a founding year.
caveat: SCOPE: GAINS is tablet software for managing Applied Behavior Analysis instruction — behavioural-therapy workflow, no neural recording or stimulation. The product launched 2017; that year must not leak in as the founding.

name: Neuro Tinker
evidence: Project page written by the founders: "Joe and Zach formed NeuroTinker, LLC to commercialize the concept on 4/15/2015."
caveat: The source is the founders’ own Hackaday project page rather than a company site. The PROJECT began mid-2012 with hardware development from February 2014; neither is the company. SCOPE: NeuroBytes are educational electronic neuron-simulator kits for classrooms.

name: Taka Apps
evidence: TAKA APPS LTD, company number SC584099, incorporated 19 December 2017, 2/2 East Broughton Place, Edinburgh EH1 3RP, SIC 72190.
caveat: An INCORPORATION date; no independent statement of when the founders began. The company was DISSOLVED on 26 March 2019, having existed about fifteen months. The name collides with several unrelated consumer apps called Taka.

name: Thervoyant
evidence: "Block and Alexander founded a UW–Madison startup called InseRT MRI in 2011, with the goal of guiding drug placements in the brain with MRI, under a license to a patent held by WARF."
caveat: The legal entity is InseRT MRI, Inc.; "TherVoyant" is a later trading name, so 2011 is the founding of the business behind the name rather than of a separate company.

name: Gradient Labs s.r.o.
evidence: Czech commercial register mirror: Gradient Labs s.r.o., IČO 04816358, date of registration 18 February 2016; no name change recorded.
conflict: Firmy.cz lists the Brno company under IČO 13094450 while rendering IČO 04816358 in the page body; whether there are two Gradient Labs entities in Brno could not be resolved, and 13094450 would imply a 2022 registration.
caveat: This is NOT the London AI customer-support company at gradientlabs.io. The index URL is a product page (SunBall) rather than the company.

name: Brain Navi Biotechnology
evidence: "Brain Navi Biotechnology, a medical robotics company founded in 2015 in Taiwan..."
caveat: The company’s own about page failed over TLS, so the year rests on a company-issued press release rather than the site itself; several independent outlets repeat 2015.

name: Qubiotech
evidence: "The company was founded in December 2014, from the transfer of an image quantification algorithm by Positron Emission Tomography (PET), developed by the Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging Research Group of the Health Research Institute Foundation from Santiago de Compostela, Spain."

name: Javelin Medical
evidence: Dealroom, Tracxn and Crunchbase all give founding year 2012, founder Guy Shinar.
caveat: Aggregator-only — no primary or news source states it, so back-derivation from an early funding round cannot be ruled out.
