The index records Estero, USA; Dun & Bradstreet and the company’s own site place it at 27 Ha-Kidma St, Yokneam Illit, Israel. SCOPE: Vine is a permanent CAROTID filter intercepting emboli in atrial fibrillation — a cardiovascular device with a stroke endpoint, not a neural interface.

name: Innoria Kft.
evidence: Nemzeti Cégtár gives founding year 2017 for Innoria Kft., company number Cg. 01-09-304074.
caveat: The registry page itself warns that no current valid data is held, so the year comes from the aggregator summary rather than a live filing. The company is listed as "v. a." — under voluntary liquidation. The 01 prefix is Budapest, not Debrecen as the index records.

name: ARM
evidence: "Arm was officially founded as a company in November 1990 as Advanced RISC Machines Ltd, which was a joint venture between Acorn Computers, Apple Computer (now Apple Inc.), and VLSI Technology (now NXP Semiconductors N.V)."
caveat: SCOPE: Arm Holdings plc is the Cambridge semiconductor IP licensing company behind the ARM instruction set. It makes no device, no neural interface and no clinical product. Note the ancestry trap: the ARM architecture dates to Acorn’s ARM1 in 1985, five years before the company existed.

name: NeuroDiagnostic Devices
evidence: A release dated 18 December 2006 announces "Neuro Diagnostic Devices (NeuroDx)... a medical device company developing innovative products to address unmet needs in the neurosurgical market", naming Frederick Fritz CEO — so the entity existed by end of 2006.
conflict: Crunchbase and secondary write-ups say founded 2008 by Fred Fritz and Dr Marek Swoboda, but the company was already operating publicly under the NeuroDx name in December 2006. A plausible reconciliation: the original Philadelphia entity dates to about 2005-2006, founded on neurosurgeon Dr Samuel Neff’s invention, and a successor entity, NeuroDx Development LLC, was formed about 2008 on spin-out from the University City Science Center.
caveat: The legal entity per SBIR.gov is NeuroDx Development LLC of Yardley, Pennsylvania; the index’s Princeton NJ address was its circa-2011 office.

name: Bionic Sight
evidence: Listed as "2013 – present", headquarters New York City, NY.
caveat: No primary source: the company’s own about page names founder Sheila Nirenberg of Weill Cornell but gives no year or address. bionic-vision.org is a curated academic resource rather than a commercial aggregator, but still not primary. The index’s location looks wrong — Gainesville FL is almost certainly the clinical trial site.

name: Quell
evidence: "The company, founded in 1996 by Shai N. Gozani as a spin-off from the Harvard-M.I.T. Division of Health Sciences and Technology, manufactures a new class of non-invasive products for point-of-care testing of neuromuscular disorders."
caveat: Quell is a PRODUCT — a wearable TENS device for chronic pain. The company is NeuroMetrix, Inc. of Waltham MA, founded June 1996, and since 2 May 2025 a wholly-owned subsidiary of electroCore, Inc. The year belongs to NeuroMetrix, not to the product.

name: AURA
evidence: Founded August 2015, 28045 Madrid, Spain; "Medical robotic solutions that are efficient, straightforward and doctor-friendly."
caveat: aurarobotix.com returned HTTP 403, so the year could not be checked against the company itself and rests on startup directories. Legal name AURA Innovative Robotics S.L., a Universidad Politécnica de Madrid spin-off; its OSCANN product is videooculography for early diagnosis of neurological disorders, so despite the generic name it is in scope.

name: Entertech (回车科技)
evidence: "Established in 2014, Entertech is a technological innovation company dedicated to acquisition, analysis, and application of brainwaves combined with other physiological signals."
caveat: The year is not on the company’s own site — entertech.cn/en/about.html states none. The "Established in 2014" wording appears verbatim across aggregators, suggesting company-supplied boilerplate: reassuring but still second-hand. Legal name Hangzhou Enter Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.

name: BKIN Technologies
evidence: "The KINARM Exoskeleton was commercialized in 2004 when BKIN Technologies was founded by Dr. Scott and Dr. Ian Brown with the assistance of PARTEQ Innovations."
caveat: The underlying KINARM exoskeleton was developed by Stephen Scott at Queen’s University’s Centre for Neuroscience Studies in 1999; that is the invention date, not the company. The company now does business as Kinarm (kinarm.com), so the index name is the older legal one.

name: Ogenblik
evidence: OGENBLIK LTD, company no. 09181146, incorporated on 19 August 2014; status dissolved on 20 May 2025.
caveat: An INCORPORATION date used as a proxy — no independent founding statement was found. The registered office is Saffron Walden, Essex, not London as the index records. ogenblikltd.com 301-redirects to olitool.com, which returns 404.

name: MED-ALLY
evidence: "In 2011, following a recapitalization at their previous employer, Raja Hitti and John Mulvihill decided to pursue new business ventures to address an unmet need in the Bioelectronic Active Implantable Medical Device arena."
caveat: The 2018 South Carolina Governor’s announcement of a new Berkeley County facility is an EXPANSION, not a founding.

name: Natus
evidence: Natus 10-K: incorporated in California in May 1987; reincorporated in Delaware in August 2000.
caveat: The corporate site’s "for more than 80 years" line is ACQUIRED-BRAND heritage (Grass, Nicolet, Bio-logic) rather than Natus’s own age, and was not used. Taken private by ArchiMed in 2022 at $33.50 a share, so no longer Nasdaq-listed; headquarters have moved to Middleton, Wisconsin, so the index’s San Carlos is stale.

name: Intendu
evidence: "an Israel-based healthcare startup co-founded in 2012 by Preminger with a mission to improve cognitive rehabilitation of people with brain dysfunction."
caveat: intendu.com still serves a full site but carries mismatched "© Copyright 2020" and "© 2021 Intendu" footers, which were not used as a year signal; current trading status could not be confirmed and the content looks stale.

name: Open Mind Neurotechnologies
evidence: The company’s own site states it was founded in 2016.
caveat: Now branded Omind; the earlier or legal name appears as Open Mind Innovation, French SIREN 818971111, a number in the 2016 range. The French registry could not be loaded to confirm. SCOPE: the current positioning is corporate leadership and soft-skills training grounded in neuroscience, not neurotechnology development.

name: Epitrack
evidence: Founded 2013 (given as 20 July 2013) by Onício Leal Neto and Jones Albuquerque, Recife, Brazil.
caveat: Aggregator-only; the Brazilian press coverage gives no founding date. NAME COLLISION: this Epitrack does participatory epidemiological surveillance, a Fiocruz spin-off — it is not an epilepsy company. "EpiTrack" is separately the name of a German neuropsychological attention test used in epilepsy, which is most likely why the row entered a neurotech index. epitrack.com.br does not resolve.

name: Bioseb
evidence: "Since 1993, Bioseb has a long tradition of leadership and innovation in the field of in-vivo research instruments"; the same history records that in 1996 Bioseb was acquired by Jacques Desevré.
conflict: The company’s own history dates the business to 1993, but the current French legal entity, SIREN 528242787 of Vitrolles, was registered in 2010 — a re-registration of an older business. 1993 is the business; 2010 is the registered company.
caveat: Neither the history page nor the French registry could be opened directly (403 and empty), so both figures come from search snippets. SCOPE: preclinical in-vivo instruments for rodents — grip strength meters, von Frey pain-threshold devices, tail suspension automation — not human neurotechnology.

name: NeuroLux
evidence: "Although NeuroLux was founded in 2015, the core technology represents the outcome of a development effort that began in the spring of 2011..."
caveat: The company’s own page deliberately separates the founding from the underlying research effort. The .org domain is a choice, not a nonprofit signal. SCOPE: preclinical rodent instrumentation — wireless optogenetics hardware out of John Rogers’ Northwestern work — rather than human neurotech.

name: Cogito Corporation
evidence: "Cogito was launched in 2007, when Feast, then a student at the MIT Sloan School of Management, took a class with Pentland."
caveat: SCOPE: real-time acoustic and linguistic voice analytics for contact-centre agent coaching, out of MIT Media Lab "honest signals" research — behavioural signal processing, not neurotechnology. Acquired by Verint Systems, closing 11 October 2024 for about $61.4M; cogitocorp.com now 301-redirects to verint.com/cogito.

name: CortexLabs
evidence: "CortexLabs is an unfunded company based in North Melbourne (Australia), founded in 2011."
caveat: Independently consistent with the company’s own blog, whose entire post history runs July to September 2011 — which is also evidence it has been dormant since. cortexlabs.com.au returns HTTP 500. Search summaries state it was founded BY Atcomm Enterprises as a separate company, which would make it a spin-out of a parent rather than an independent founding; that could not be verified. Not to be confused with Cortical Labs, the unrelated Melbourne DishBrain company.

name: Bpaus
evidence: Startup Nation Finder profile: founded February 2019, founders Yuri Tselicov and Evgeny Borovsky.
caveat: Startup Nation Central returned 403 to direct fetch, so the year comes from the indexed summary; Crunchbase and PitchBook carry the same February 2019. SCOPE: clinical practice-management and assessment software for autism diagnosis and therapy tracking, sold to clinics — health SaaS, not neurotechnology.

name: CogSci Apps Corp.
evidence: "In 2014, I also spun-off some of CogZest’s intellectual property portfolio to a new startup co-founded by Brian Shi and myself, CogSci Apps Corp."
caveat: A first-person statement by co-founder Luc P. Beaudoin on the parent company’s own site. SCOPE: consumer software — Hook/Hookmark, a macOS productivity tool, and mySleepButton, a "cognitive shuffle" audio app. No sensing, stimulation or neural data anywhere in the product line.
